On Saturday I actually heard a Democratic analyst/operative on MSNBC make a point contrasting Platner and Ken Paxton, who Democratic talking heads keep trying to tie together over supposed moral turpitude. His point was that Paxton at least had a record of accomplishment as an elected official that his voters could support whereas Platner hadn’t accomplished anything nor overcome anything. 

Let that sink in for a moment. 

The Texas GOP tried to impeach Paxton for corruption. Take a quick look at the 20 years of Paxton scandals or at his freakish relationship with Nate Paul. 

To Democratic operatives these represent things Paxton has going for him over Platner? Are we in the upside down? I also think the glib dismissal of Platner’s military service is telling. Corporate lawyer defending large multinationals or a prosecutor contributing to mass incarceration is good experience. Whereas, enlisting in the military and serving 4 tours in war is to be dismissed out of hand. Having experience not as a member of a protected professional class but as a normal working person, isn’t an asset, it’s disqualifying. 

The mainstream of both parties has nothing but distain for working class people and military veterans, except of course when they need convenient props, then it’s all about firefighters, nurses, teachers and soldiers. 

There’s something profound going on here. Platner hasn’t done himself any favors but the organized effort to stop this man from reaching the Senate by people in his own party and the so-called liberal media is something to behold, given the usual threshold for scandal coverage over your average politicians. It’s made even more jarring considering the massive groundwell of support amongst Mainers. You’d almost get the impression that it’s all the regular working people supporting Platner, that they’re really worried about.
